messages:
molly: heads-up — canary for the gptx-3.1-checkpoint onboarding is blocked. p99 spiked ~35% and throughput dropped ~28% after the model bump. seeing this only in eu-west canary :warning:

arun: ugh. was anything else merged around the same time (tokenizer, runtimes, quant libs)?

megan: quick profile from the canary box (short):
```
kernel_selector: selected kernel fast_gemm_fused for 64x48
kernel_selector: fallback to MatMulFallback for 128x96 (reason: unsupported rotary dim 64 != 32)
jit: recompile kernels for model=gptx-3.1-checkpoint variant=v2.1
latency: p99 increase correlates with kernel fallback + jit recompile
```

jamie: also looked at input shapes. tokenizer produces ~1.4x more tokens for a few prompts because a separator token is split into 2 tokens by the new vocab mapping. effective sequence length shifted from ~120 -> ~170 on common queries, which pushes batching heuristics to much smaller batch sizes.

ryan: adding KV cache traces — we see repeated cache reinitialization and misses when incoming seq_len changes per request:
```
kv_cache: found existing cache key for session but seq_len mismatch (old=128, new=170) -> recreate cache
kv_cache: cache entries flushed for model gptx-3.1-checkpoint:v2.1
```

molly: ok bisect plan: i ran a quick git-log around the onboarding PRs. suspect commits: 3b7f2d (tokenizer mapping change), a9c4f1 (model card metadata), d2f8b0 (runtime kernel selector tweak). i'm going to trigger CI perf jobs for each commit in isolation. @ci-bot can you run perf-smoke/gptx-3.1 with baseline v2.0 and bumped v2.1?

ci-bot: started perf job -> https://ci.example/redwood/jobs/7623
ci-bot: results (smoke):
```
baseline (v2.0): p50=18ms p95=46ms p99=72ms qps=125
onboard (v2.1): p50=20ms p95=59ms p99=97ms qps=90
delta: p99 +34ms (+47%), qps -28%
```

arun: that delta is huge. my money's on the tokenizer split + kernel selector not tolerating slightly larger rotary dims / seq shapes. quick mitigation: revert tokenizer mapping in the onboarding branch or add a compatibility mapping that maps the separator token back to one token pre-serve. also we should relax kernel selector fallbacks to tolerate rotary-dim mismatches where safe.

jamie: i implemented a proof-of-concept shim that maps the new separator token to the old single token at runtime (no model weight change). reran perf locally:
```
with shim: p99=74ms qps=120
```
which is roughly baseline.

megan: excellent. follow-ups: (1) add a unit test that runs tokenization -> batching heuristic path to detect tokenization regressions (2) add a perf gating step on model onboarding that runs the smoke suite and enforces p99 within 10% or fallback (3) update kernel selector tests to include small rotary-dim deltas and ensure we don't fallback to slow matmul unless necessary.

molly: agreed. i'm going to request a rollback of the canary and keep the onboarding PR blocked until we ship the shim + tests. @deploy-bot schedule a rollback to v2.0 for eu-west canary, please.

deploy-bot: rollback to gptx-3.1-checkpoint:v2.0 scheduled at 2025-03-14T18:20Z. action: canary rolled back. :white_check_mark:

molly: thanks. action items assigned: jamie to land the runtime tokenizer shim (hotfix), megan to add perf-gate tests + kernel-selector unit tests, arun to propose selector tolerance thresholds, ryan to add KV-cache seq_len-compat warning and metrics. will keep this thread until tasks are merged and canary is re-run.

arun: quick note — if we end up needing a permanent fix in kernel selection, we should add a short path that detects only dim mismatch and picks nearest optimized kernel rather than full fallback. precision tests will be needed though.

megan: logging follow-up: i've captured a perf trace exported to s3://perf-traces/gptx-3.1/1769234567.tar.gz for postmortem.

molly: closing loop — shim merged to staging, perf-smoke passed, rolling canary back up once stable. will follow up with a short postmortem in #postmortems. thanks everyone.
